chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Only the one who recognizes God, Mighty and Majestic, and worships Him truly — that is, the one who recognizes God and recognizes his Imam from us, the People of the Household.

And whoever does not recognize God, Mighty and Majestic, and does not recognize the Imam from us, the People of the Household, then he is only recognizing and worshipping other than God. Thus, by God, is the straying!'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: People of the Household — the Prophet's family and the Imams
key_terms.إِنَّمَا: Only/none but — a restrictive particle indicating exclusive condition
key_terms.ضَلَالًا: Straying, misguidance — the condition of one who lacks recognition of the Imam
key_terms.يَعْبُدُهُ: Worships Him — true worship (ibada) accepted by God
key_terms.يَعْرِفُ اللَّهَ: Recognizes/knows God — in Shia theology, this is ma'rifa (gnosis), not mere factual knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about recognizing God and the Imam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) makes a definitive doctrinal statement: true recognition of God and true worship of Him are inseparable from recognizing the Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt. This hadith, reported by Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi — a close companion of the Imam — establishes that mere verbal acknowledgment of God without accepting the divinely appointed Imam constitutes a form of polytheism or deviation. The statement uses the emphatic particle 'innama' to restrict true ma'rifa (gnosis) and worship exclusively to those who combine recognition of God with recognition of the Imam, making this one of the cornerstone hadiths of Shia creedal theology on the imamate.
